outcome: Actively treated physician-diagnosed depression/severe anxiety at 3 years
cohort: 15,936 women in the UK Millennium Cohort Study who gave birth between 2000-2002
finding: Women with long-standing depression or anxiety who had elective caesarean had a lower risk of postnatal distress, but a greater risk of actively treated depression/anxiety at 3 years if they had an emergency caesarean.
mod_finding: Women with long-standing depression/anxiety had a lower risk of PPD following elective caesarean compared to vaginal birth, and a higher risk of actively treated depression/anxiety at 3 years following emergency caesarean compared to vaginal birth.
